## Moist adiabat extrapolation with the effective heat capacity (`extrapolate_dlnp`, `extrapolate_dz`) {#sec-ch03-adiabat}

### Summary

An initial atmosphere is often built by lifting a parcel along an adiabat: entropy is held fixed while pressure
falls, and condensates form when vapours saturate. `ThermoX` provides this step. Given $(T, p, x)$ at one level,
`extrapolate_dlnp` moves to a new pressure and `extrapolate_dz` to a new height under hydrostatic balance, and both
return the temperature and equilibrated composition there. The temperature is found by a Newton iteration whose
slope is the effective heat capacity, the ordinary heat capacity plus the latent heat released per kelvin by
condensation that keeps the parcel saturated. This follows the multi-condensable moist adiabat of Li, Ingersoll and Oyafuso (2018,
[doi:10.1175/JAS-D-17-0257.1](https://doi.org/10.1175/JAS-D-17-0257.1)).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Hold the molar entropy at its target, @eq-ch03-adiabat-target, using the slope
@eq-ch03-adiabat-cpeff.

**Data.** $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], $x_n$ [-] in and out (overwritten); $\Delta \ln p$ [-] or $\Delta z$ [m] and $g$
[m s$^{-2}$].

**Placement.** API calls, typically one per level when building a column.

**Activation.** `extrapolate_dlnp(temp, pres, xfrac, dlnp, ...)`, `extrapolate_dz(temp, pres, xfrac, dz, grav,
...)`; `rainout` default off.

**Guarantee / limits.** Reversible: $\bar s$ held, no step error in $\ln p$. Rain-out: first order in $\Delta \ln p$. In $z$:
trapezoidal hydrostatics.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\bar s$, entropy per mole of mixture, gas and condensate [J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; $\bar c_p$, frozen
heat capacity per mole of mixture [J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; $\bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}$, effective heat capacity per
mole of mixture [J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; $\xi_r$, extent of reaction $r$ per mole of mixture [-]; $\mathsf G$, the
gain matrix of the saturation adjustment at fixed $T$ and $p$ (@sec-ch04) [-]; $\Delta h_r = \sum_n \nu_{nr} h_n$
[J mol$^{-1}$]; $\bar\mu$, mean molar mass of the mixture [kg mol$^{-1}$]; $g$, gravitational acceleration,
positive [m s$^{-2}$]; $\Delta z$, height change, positive upward [m]; $\nu_{nr}$ and $c_{p,n}$ as in
@sec-ch03-species-functions. Symbols of the notation table (@sec-appa): $K_r$, $h_n$, $x_n$, $c_n$, $x_{\mathrm g}$, $N_{\mathrm g}$.

### Derivation

**The dry limit: Poisson's law.** Start with nothing condensing. The question is what the routine reduces to and how
that connects to the potential temperature. With no active reaction the gain matrix is empty and the heat capacity is
the frozen $\bar c_p = \sum_n x_n c_{p,n}$ (`effective_cp`,
{{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::effective_cp >}}). For an ideal-gas mixture of fixed composition
and constant heat capacities, the molar entropy is $\bar s = \bar c_p \ln T - \mathcal R \ln p + \text{const}$
(@eq-ch03-species-functions-sgas, summed with the mole fractions; the mixing terms are constant at fixed
composition). Setting $\mathrm d \bar s = 0$ and integrating from $(T_0, p_0)$ gives

$$
T_1 = T_0 \exp\!\left(\frac{\mathcal R}{\bar c_p}\, \Delta \ln p\right) , \qquad
\theta = T \left(\frac{p_0}{p}\right)^{\mathcal R/\bar c_p} \ \text{unchanged} ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-poisson}

Poisson's law, with $\theta$ the potential temperature referred to $p_0$. The update of the routine (below) with
$\bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}} = \bar c_p$ is $T \leftarrow T [1 + \ln(T_1/T)]$ at the new pressure. Its fixed point is $T_1$,
and the derivative of the map there is $1 - 1 = 0$, so it converges quadratically to @eq-ch03-adiabat-poisson. kintera
has no separate potential-temperature function at the pin. With condensation there is no single potential
temperature to conserve: the conserved quantity is the molar entropy of the saturated parcel, derived next.

**Effective heat capacity.** Hold $p$ fixed and let $T$ change by $\mathrm d T$ in a saturated parcel. The frozen
part of the enthalpy change per mole of mixture is $\bar c_p\, \mathrm d T$ with $\bar c_p = \sum_n x_n c_{p,n}$.
The reaction extents change too, by $\mathrm d \xi_r$, releasing $-\Delta h_r\, \mathrm d \xi_r$. Saturation is
kept: each active reaction's log quotient, formed from the gas mole fractions $x_n / x_{\mathrm g}$ with sums over
gases only (@sec-ch04), follows its log saturation constant at fixed $p$, so with $\mathsf G$ the derivative of
the log quotients with respect to the extents,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf G\, \frac{\mathrm d \boldsymbol\xi}{\mathrm d T} &= \frac{\mathrm d \ln \mathbf K}{\mathrm d T}, \\
\bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}} &= \sum_n x_n c_{p,n} + \sum_r \Delta h_r \frac{\mathrm d \xi_r}{\mathrm d T} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-cpeff}

@eq-ch03-adiabat-cpeff is computed in `effective_cp`
({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::effective_cp >}}). Before solving the first line, the code
divides each row of $\mathsf G$ and of the right side by that row's largest magnitude, which leaves the solution
unchanged in exact arithmetic and lowers the condition number. The solve is a least-squares solve (`gelsd`) on CPU
and a pseudo-inverse with absolute tolerance $10^{-6}$ on CUDA. Inactive reactions have zero rows and get zero
$\mathrm d\xi_r/\mathrm d T$. Without a gain matrix (no reactions) the function returns $\bar c_p$.

**Entropy target.** The parcel's molar entropy is $\bar s = S / \sum_n c_n$, with $S$ of
@eq-ch03-thermo-x-totals, the entropy per mole of mixture, gas and condensate together. The reversible step keeps
$\bar s$; a user-supplied rate adds a prescribed change. Holding $\bar s$ is holding the total entropy only when the
total number of moles is unchanged by the condensation. That is true for a reaction with one mole of vapour per
mole of condensate, such as H$_2$O to H$_2$O(l), but not for NH$_3$ + H$_2$S to NH$_4$SH(s), which turns two moles
into one. For a closed parcel with conserved dry gas, the total entropy per mole of dry gas, $\bar s / x_0$, is the
conserved quantity, so the reversible target would be $\bar s_0\, x_0^{\mathrm{new}} / x_0^{\mathrm{old}}$; the
code applies that factor only in the rain-out branch below (verified by reading `extrapolate_dlnp` at the pin). The
resulting error has not been measured. The targets are:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bar s_{\mathrm{target}} &= \bar s_0 + \frac{\mathrm d \bar s}{\mathrm d \ln p}\, \Delta \ln p , \\
\bar s_{\mathrm{target}} &= \bar s_0 + \frac{\mathrm d \bar s}{\mathrm d z}\, \Delta z ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-target}

the first line for `extrapolate_dlnp` and the second for `extrapolate_dz`, with the rates the arguments `ds_dlnp`
and `ds_dz` (default 0). Both functions compute their target at entry.

**The entropy slope along the saturated path.** The Newton step needs $\mathrm d \bar s/\mathrm d T$ along the
saturated path at fixed $p$. For a closed parcel (fixed element amounts) the fundamental relation at fixed $p$ is
$\mathrm d H = T\, \mathrm d S + \sum_n \mu_n\, \mathrm d \mathcal N_n$, with $\mu_n = h_n - T s_n$ the molar Gibbs
energy.
Along the saturated path every active reaction stays at zero Gibbs energy, $\sum_n \nu_{nr} \mu_n = 0$
(@sec-ch03-species-functions), and the amounts change only through the extents,
$\mathrm d \mathcal N_n = \sum_r \nu_{nr}\, \mathrm d \xi_r$, so the last term vanishes:

$$
\mathrm d H = T\, \mathrm d S \quad \text{(closed parcel, fixed } p \text{, equilibrium path)} .
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-gibbs}

This also needs each species to satisfy its own Gibbs relation, $\mathrm d h_n = T\, \mathrm d s_n$ at fixed $p$. That
holds for the gases, and for a condensate whose entropy is solved from saturation only when its card matches its
curve (@eq-ch03-reference-state-sc-slope). Per mole of mixture, with $n$ moles in the parcel,
$T\, \mathrm d(S/n) = \mathrm d(H/n) + (H - T S)\, \mathrm d n / n^2$. When the condensation leaves $n$ unchanged
(one vapour mole per condensate mole) this is
$T\, \mathrm d \bar s = \mathrm d \bar h = \bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}\, \mathrm d T$:

$$
\frac{\mathrm d \bar s}{\mathrm d T} = \frac{\bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}}{T} .
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-dsdt}

When $n$ changes (NH$_4$SH forms from two gas moles), the slope depends on which heat capacity is meant.
`effective_cp` ({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::effective_cp >}}) returns
$\sum_n x_n c_{p,n} + \sum_r \Delta h_r\, \mathrm d \xi_r/\mathrm d T$, which is $(1/n)\, \mathrm d H/\mathrm d T$ for
the
parcel, not $\mathrm d \bar h/\mathrm d T$. With that quantity, $T\, \mathrm d S = \mathrm d H$ and $S = n \bar s$ give

$$
\frac{\mathrm d \bar s}{\mathrm d T} = \frac{\bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}}{T}
- \bar s\, \frac{\mathrm d \ln n}{\mathrm d T} .
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-dsdt-n}

Where NH4SH forms (NH3 = H2S = $5 \times 10^{-3}$ in dry gas, 170-240 K, $10^5$ Pa), `effective_cp` equals a central
difference of $(1/n)\, \mathrm d H/\mathrm d T$ to $6.8 \times 10^{-8}$ and differs from $\mathrm d \bar h/\mathrm d T$
by up
to $3.6 \times 10^{-3}$ (check line `(h4)`). The step below uses the slope of @eq-ch03-adiabat-dsdt even then, which
changes the rate of the iteration but not its fixed point.

**Temperature update in $\ln p$.** At the new pressure, Newton's method on $\bar s(T) = \bar s_{\mathrm{target}}$ with
the slope @eq-ch03-adiabat-dsdt, written in relative form, is

$$
T \leftarrow T \left(1 + \frac{\bar s_{\mathrm{target}} - \bar s(T)}{\bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}}\right) ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-newton}

computed in `extrapolate_dlnp` ({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dlnp >}}).

**Hydrostatic step in $z$.** For a step $\Delta z$, the pressure follows the trapezoidal rule of
$\mathrm d p / \mathrm d z = -\rho g$:

$$
p_1 = p_0 - \tfrac12 (\rho_0 + \rho_1)\, g\, \Delta z .
$$ {#eq-ch03-adiabat-hydrostatic}

The temperature update adds the change of $\bar s$ caused by the pressure change of this iteration,
$-x_{\mathrm g} \mathcal R\, \Delta \ln p$ for ideal gases, with $x_{\mathrm g}$ of @sec-ch03-eos:

$$
T \leftarrow T \left(1 + \frac{\bar s_{\mathrm{target}} - \bar s + x_{\mathrm g} \mathcal R\, \Delta \ln p}
{\bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}}\right) .
$$

The first pressure guess is isothermal, $p = p_0 \exp(-g \bar\mu \Delta z / (\mathcal R T))$. Both updates are in
`extrapolate_dz` ({{< code src/thermo/extrapolate_ad.cpp ThermoXImpl::extrapolate_dz >}}).

**Pseudo-adiabat.** With `rainout`, the condensate formed in the step leaves the parcel and carries its entropy
with it. Per mole of the conserved dry gas, the target becomes

$$
\bar s_{\mathrm{target}} = \frac{x_0^{\mathrm{new}}}{x_0^{\mathrm{old}}}\, \bar s_0
- \frac{\sum_{m \ge N_{\mathrm g}} s_m c_m}{\sum_{n < N_{\mathrm g}} c_n} + (\text{prescribed change}) ,
$$

with $s_m$ the condensate entropy of @eq-ch03-species-functions-scond, and the condensate mole fractions are set to
zero and the rest renormalised. The target is evaluated once, at the end state: all the condensate formed over the
step is removed with its end-state entropy $s_m(T_1, p_1)$ (verified by reading `extrapolate_dlnp` at the pin). The
continuous pseudo-adiabat obeys $\mathrm d(n_{\mathrm g} \bar s_{\mathrm g}) = -\sum_m s_m\, \mathrm d n_m$, with
$s_m$ varying along the path; evaluating $s_m$ at one end of the step is the one-sided rectangle rule for that
integral, whose error is first order in $\Delta \ln p$. So the rain-out target, unlike the reversible one, depends
on the step size.

What is exact and what is truncated: the reversible step of `extrapolate_dlnp` (no `rainout`) has no truncation error
in $\Delta \ln p$; its end state satisfies $\bar s(T, p_1) = \bar s_{\mathrm{target}}$ to within 10 times `ftol`, in
J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, whatever the step; $\bar s$ is the parcel's total entropy only when the condensation leaves
the number of moles unchanged (see the entropy target above). With `rainout` the step has the first-order error of the rectangle rule
above, measured by check line `(h3)`: for $\Delta \ln p = -0.2$ from 300 K and 10 bar, the end temperature with
$N$ = 4, 8, 16, 32 steps differs from the $N = 512$ result by $7.52 \times 10^{-2}$, $3.73 \times 10^{-2}$,
$1.84 \times 10^{-2}$ and $8.88 \times 10^{-3}$ K, observed orders 1.012, 1.023 and 1.048. `extrapolate_dz` adds the
trapezoidal error of @eq-ch03-adiabat-hydrostatic, second order in $\Delta z$ for a smooth $\rho(z)$ (a standard
property of the trapezoidal rule; no test measures it).

### Numerical method

Each call runs a fixed-point loop of at most `max_iter` iterations. In every iteration it: (1) resets $x$ to the
input composition; (2) runs the saturation adjustment `forward` at the current $(T, p)$, which returns $\mathsf G$;
(3) with `rainout`, forms the pseudo-adiabatic target and removes the condensates; (4) evaluates
$\bar c_p^{\mathrm{eff}}$ and $\bar s$; (5) stops if $\max \lvert \bar s_{\mathrm{target}} - \bar s \rvert$ is below 10 times `ftol`;
(6) updates $T$ (and, in `extrapolate_dz`, first $p$). The convergence test is a maximum over all cells. If the loop
ends without meeting it, a warning is printed and the last iterate is returned.

The adiabat figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

: Code map of the adiabat extrapolation. {#tbl-ch03-adiabat-code}

Warnings a user can hit: "extrapolate_dlnp does not converge after N iterations" and "extrapolate_ad does not
converge after N iterations" (the second is printed by `extrapolate_dz`). The `verbose` option prints the state of
every iteration. Both functions overwrite `temp`, `pres` and `xfrac` in place.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_thermo.release` (`DeviceTest.extrapolate_ad`) | molar entropy unchanged after a step $\Delta \ln p = -0.1$ | $10^{-3}$ rel. and abs. | not yet derived |
| `test_earth.py` | a 2-D column built by `extrapolate_dlnp` runs | none | smoke test, no assertion |
| `test_python_subprocess` (`test_effective_cp_heap_state.py`) | CPU `effective_cp` is the same whatever the heap held, in one cell and in a batch, and exceeds the frozen $\bar c_p$ | exact equality | bitwise reproducibility by design |

: Tests of the adiabat extrapolation. {#tbl-ch03-adiabat-tests}

`DeviceTest.extrapolate_ad` is skipped in float32 and runs in float64 on CPU and on CUDA when a GPU is present.
`tests/test_effective_cp_heap_state.py` asserts that `effective_cp` on CPU gives one value whatever the heap holds
and keeps the latent term. It runs in CTest inside the single entry `test_python_subprocess`, which runs the
`subprocess_tests` list of `tests/CMakeLists.txt` at the pin, and so in the CI of kintera (`ctest --output-on-failure`).
`test_jupiter_tp_adiabat.py` builds a deep adiabat with repeated `forward` calls and its own temperature bracket; it
does not call `extrapolate_dlnp` or `extrapolate_dz`, so it is not evidence for this section. No kintera test covers
`extrapolate_dz`, `rainout`, or the trapezoidal order.

The derivation is checked by two derivation checks. `check_ch3_adiabat.py`:[^ch03-adiabat-check]

- `4a`: the dry limit @eq-ch03-adiabat-poisson. A dry parcel stepped by $\Delta \ln p = -0.5$ ends within
  $2.0 \times 10^{-9}$ of $300 \exp(-0.5\, \mathcal R/\bar c_p)$ at `ftol` $10^{-6}$, and within 0 at $10^{-12}$
  (tolerance $10^{-8}$).
- `4b`: @eq-ch03-adiabat-cpeff, `effective_cp` = 31.3465 J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at 280 K and 10 bar, against a central
  difference of the equilibrium molar enthalpy, $3.4 \times 10^{-9}$. A saturated reversible step
  $\Delta \ln p = -0.01$ changes $\bar s$ by $4.6 \times 10^{-7}$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ (tolerance $10^{-5}$).

`check_ch3_adiabat_slope.py`:[^ch03-adiabat-slope-check]

- `(h1)`: @eq-ch03-adiabat-gibbs for a closed parcel at 280 K and 10 bar (per mole of dry gas). With the cards of
  `tests/jupiter.yaml` $T\, \mathrm d S/\mathrm d T$ and $\mathrm d H/\mathrm d T$ differ by $2.2 \times 10^{-3}$,
  because the solved condensate entropies fail their Gibbs relation, EXPECTED-FAIL (K8). With the cards of
  @eq-ch03-reference-state-card they agree to $2.3 \times 10^{-10}$.
- `(h2)`: $\mathrm d \bar h/\mathrm d T$ along the path equals `effective_cp` to $3.4 \times 10^{-9}$.
- `(h4)`: where NH4SH forms, `effective_cp` equals $(1/n)\, \mathrm d H/\mathrm d T$ to $6.8 \times 10^{-8}$
  (@eq-ch03-adiabat-dsdt-n), and differs from $\mathrm d \bar h/\mathrm d T$ by up to $3.6 \times 10^{-3}$.
- `(h3)`: the rain-out branch is first order in $\Delta \ln p$, observed orders 1.012-1.048 (tolerance 0.15 on the
  order).

### Limits

`extrapolate_dz` is untested. With `rainout`, a column built in steps of $\Delta \ln p$ carries a first-order step
error (Derivation, check line `(h3)`); this is the documented accuracy limit K5, not a code defect; a precipitating copy
of a condensate that has no nucleation reaction of its own
leaves with zero entropy (@sec-ch03-species-functions). The CUDA path of `effective_cp` uses an absolute pseudo-inverse
tolerance of $10^{-6}$ on the row-scaled matrix, while the CPU path uses `gelsd`; whether the two agree on
ill-conditioned gain matrices is not measured. The entropy target uses the constant-$c_p$ gas entropy of
@sec-ch03-species-functions, so with `use-nasa9-cp` the step conserves that entropy, not the NASA-9 one (K6; the size
of the effect on the adiabat is not measured).
